artworks.name: Born Of Burn
artworks.description:
After a fire, what remains is never the same as what went in.
When the heat fades and everything goes quiet, something slowly begins to return.

These flowers don’t belong to gardens.
They come from burned ground, from places shaped by loss and endurance at the same time.
Ash becomes their soil.
Leftover heat traces their beginnings.

They carry the memory of what happened here,
and they remind me that beauty can exist even after damage.
artworks.materials: Ponderosa pine, burned wood pieces, acrylic on canvas

artworks.name: By Marks and Fire
artworks.description:
Experience doesn’t come gently.
It scalds, splits, leaves gold in its wake.

What stays behind is proof 
of mistakes, of survival,
of becoming something textured,
something true.
artworks.materials: Old acacia, oak catkins, Bohemian truffle pigment, acrylic on canvas

artworks.name: Core

It’s where it all begins.

artworks.name: July Pines
artworks.description:
There was a forest that watched me grow.
Twelve summers in a row, I returned — first as a child, then as a mother.
It held my laughter, my tears, my friendships, my first love.

Now, the place that shaped so much of me is gone. Unreachable, unsafe.

But I still carry the scent of pine, the feel of the earth, the hush of the trees.

This work is a memory in texture. 
A quiet longing.
A piece of what I never want to forget.
artworks.materials: Acacia bark, algae, river sand, bohemian truffle, fresh grass pigment, acrylic on canvas

artworks.name: Moonglow
artworks.materials: Air plant, acrylic on canvas

artworks.name: Navy of the Dreamland
artworks.description:
There’s a moment between sleep and waking when the forest starts to feel like the sea.
Leaves lift like small sails.
Twigs and stems stand tall, almost like masts.
Even the lace feels like foam — light, quiet, passing.

This piece came from that in-between state.
It isn’t about direction or arrival, just drifting — held by memory and a sense of quiet wonder.
artworks.materials: Acrylic, breadfruit leaves, Ming Aralia leaves, Acacia branches, textile on canvas

artworks.name: Of Ash and Flowers
artworks.description:
Some things really do bloom straight through the burn.
This piece is about what quietly comes back after an ending — when something has been stripped down, scorched, undone, and still life finds a way to return.

The textures come from real petals and plants I collected, dried, and preserved. I placed them the way memories tend to settle — not perfectly, but intentionally.

The dark areas aren’t just shadow. They’re the kind of silence that stays after fire has passed.
And the gold? It might be hope. Or it might just be the way light eventually finds its way in.
artworks.materials: Acrylic, casting medium, hydrangea flowers on canvas

artworks.name: Prolisok
artworks.description: A place on Earth of my happy summers.

artworks.name: Rise in Blue
artworks.description:
There’s something about stillness that feels important.
These petals were once soft and open. Now they stand almost like markers — lifted upward, worn by time but not broken, set against a washed blue background. Quiet, but not passive.

This piece isn’t about dramatic survival. It’s about the kind that happens quietly — in small acts of holding on. In fragile things that keep their form. In decay that still leans toward the light.
artworks.materials: Monstera stipules, araucaria, buttonbush, Bohemian truffle pigment, and acrylic

artworks.name: Spectral
artworks.description:
Shadows stretch tall in the quiet between worlds.
Golden threads drip like echoes, as if something just passed through. 
Not seen, only felt.

It lingers in the roots, in the rot,
in the places where the veil is thin.
artworks.materials:
Carpathian chaga, moss, spruce branch, 
lichen, acrylic on canvas

artworks.name: Whales
artworks.description:
A quiet protest.
Raw and restrained.
Inspired by the weight of captivity pressed on creatures meant to roam the deepest blues.
Their forms drift across pale currents, bound not by nature, but by hands that forgot how to listen.
artworks.materials:
Driftwood, jute rope, acrylic, ink,
 acrylic on canvas

artworks.name: Winds
artworks.description:
The air feels thin and fragile.
Bare branches stretch upward, almost tired,
outlined against a sky that’s lost its warmth.

There’s no storm here, no drama —
just a quiet stillness that settles in.
Not emptiness, more like a pause.
Not an ending, just waiting.

The cold doesn’t cut.
It passes through gently,
leaving behind something you can feel,
even if you don’t have a name for it.
artworks.materials: Thorny branch, ink, acrylic on canvas

artworks.name: Spring Fire
artworks.description:
It begins with a whisper.
Nature waking slowly, brushing off the last frost, dreaming of dandelions and light.
Tiny first messengers move through the hush: a beetle, a melt, a yellow bloom.

And then the world splits open.
A blaze, wild and vengeful, turning air to ash, green to black.
Even the sky forgets how to hold still.

For a while, silence feels like loss.
But beneath the burn, roots remember.

Life is patient.
What seems lost is only waiting.
And when it returns, it rises hungry, wild, and full of fire-fed strength.

This work holds part of that story -
crafted around a redwood root from a centuries-old tree that did not survive the flames, but still speaks through form, colour and texture.
artworks.materials: Red wood root piece, burned wood pigment, burned wood pieces, acrylic on canvas.

artworks.name: Mermaid's Dream
artworks.description:
She wakes in a place where the land doesn’t quite know what it is yet —
roots tangled with seafoam, thoughts drifting like seaweed.

There’s no name for her, no voice.
Just the steady pull of the tide.

She collects small flashes from broken skies and bits of foam,
weaves them into vines,
lays them gently over rust-colored ground.

What she makes can’t really be held.
It only stays with you —
later, when the air smells like salt and rain.
artworks.materials:
Bull kelp, ocean sand, burned wood and bohemian truffle pigments, 
acrylic on canvas

artworks.name: Fragments of Light
artworks.description:
This work is dedicated to the loss of Iryna Tsybukh — a figure whose courage, honesty, and love of life became a symbol for many in Ukraine.

Though she was taken by the war, the values she lived by cannot be erased.
As Iryna wrote, “To have the strength to be free, one must be brave.”

The piece reflects the emotional weight of losing something monumental — something that should not have disappeared. Fragments of Iryna’s words appear in the background, carrying the strength and inspiration she shared with others.

The colors speak of hope and freedom — of what endures, and of what continues to live in our hearts.
The textures reflect how deeply grief can tear through the soul.
artworks.materials: Sago palm seed coating, algae, sand, acrylic on canvas panel

artworks.name: November Forest
artworks.materials: Bark, sand, acrylic on canvas

artworks.name: Their Shore

Where the sea holds no questions.
Just space — soft, steady, and safe.
artworks.materials: Eastern cottonwood tree bark, algae, river sand, bohemian truffle, viscum, oak and sweet gum tree catkins, acrylic on canvas

artworks.name: The place that Stays
artworks.description:
Not everything holds.
most things shift, crack, move, disappear.
but sometimes, something stays.

This piece is about that —
a place untouched while everything else pulls apart.
the quiet in the middle of the mess.
the bark, the earth, the still green shape —
they hold their ground.

It's not about peace, not exactly.
it's about presence.
about stillness that doesn't run.
artworks.materials: Eastern cottonwood tree bark, algae, river sand, bohemian truffle, viscum, oak and sweet gum tree catkins, acrylic on canvas
